bucket_reason: Priority call: the mechanism is at medium confidence (rounds ruled, the eat not), so proof work waits for Dennis (CLAUDE.md). Only the observe pass has run; no deepen pass yet.
question: #29's rounds, overflow and marker are ruled (99.7% of K-transitions to 1e10), but the grid-shifting eat is not. Spend one ~2 h deepen stage ruling the eat, or park #29 as STUCK?

options.label: Fund one ~2 h deepen stage on the eat
options.consequence: The agent turns the eat events to 1e10 (already dumped in data/kscan_eats_1e10.txt) and the 334 shifted carries into unit-word rewrites. It fits a unit-level transducer: grid re-read 100->010, 000->000, 010->001, then the mini-eats. It then fuzzes a candidate reachable-word language for closure. Exit: if the language is closed, proof.md comes back to you at medium-high confidence. If mini-eat safety depends on the counter's bits (about N mod 2^D) non-locally, #29 is flagged under the cryptid protocol and parked.

options.label: The same stage, run jointly with sibling R2 (F0 = 0LD)
options.consequence: One analysis for both bell-eats-counter siblings. R2 shares R1/R3/R4/R5 but fails the marker step R7 (0/20) and is itself at low confidence, so the eat work would probably split in two. Expect about 2 stages instead of 1.

options.label: Park #29 as STUCK (stage observe)
options.consequence: No compute. Status becomes STUCK with the eat as the stuck point. The 11 validated rules and the K-moment dump stay for a later family pass, and the slot goes to machines with fewer unknowns.

rationale: Everything except the eat is exact. ROUND matches 870,221 of 872,741 K-transitions with 0 mismatches, OVERFLOW matches 2,382/2,382, and the right half is tm108's proven HR1/HR2/HR3/HE2. The eat is only 0.29% of transitions, but it is the whole proof problem. Random eats over the four unit types halt about 5% of the time, so the invariant has to be the reachable language, and nobody has written that down yet. #29 has had only the observe pass. #18, the other bell-eats-counter machine in this queue, closed its eat for aligned counters in its first deepen round with block-level rewrite rules, the same kind of rules this stage would fit. The cryptid risk (the eat consumes N mod 2^D) is real but untested, and a deepen stage is the cheapest way to settle it. Parking now would shelve a nearly ruled machine. Joint work with R2 is not worth it yet: R2's marker step differs, and R2's own decision proposes its own stage.

evidence.text: K-moment coverage from blank to 1e10: 872,741 transitions, 870,221 exactly ROUND, 0 mismatches. Not ruled: 1,756 after b = 0 eats, 430 mini-eats, 334 carries into shifted segments. No halt.

11 rules checked by direct simulation on random instances (seed 20261010): R1-R8 60/60 each, ROUND 372/372 with the exact step formula, OVERFLOW 150/150, EAT shape on aligned W 400/400 (shape only, not exact).
Random eat inputs that contain 001 units often halt. Banning the 100-001 pair still leaves 29 of 542 halting, so the safe language is finer than a ban on unit bigrams.

Only E1 differs from BECv1 tm108 (verify/BECv1_6x2_solved.v:872), and its HR1/HR2/HR3/HE2 hold here as R1/R7/R3/R8. solve_BECv1 cannot express the 3-cell digits or the grid shift; the closest proof styles are BECv7/BECv8.
One eat, step by step (steps 19,500-20,399): the marker walks into the counter, eats near step 19,830, then the head runs to the right end and the marker is reborn.
The cryptid check is undecided. The eat consumes the counter's bit pattern at eat time (about N mod 2^D), and if later mini-eat safety depends on those bits, the cryptid protocol applies.
Sibling R2 (F0 = 0LD) is at CHECKPOINT_A with low confidence. It passes R1/R3/R4/R5 but fails R7, so its eat is a different problem; its own decision recommends a separate deepen stage.

effort_if_yes: One ~2 h deepen stage with 1-2 heavy processes. It reuses data/kscan_eats_1e10.txt, so no new long runs are needed, and there is no Rocq work. It returns either a proof.md go/no-go or a park/cryptid flag.
